title: Count primes
statement: Return the number of primes strictly less than n (n ≤ 5 × 10⁶).
hints: Trial division per number is O(n√n).
Sieve: for each prime p, cross out p², p² + p, …; start at p² because smaller multiples were crossed out by smaller primes.

solution.explanation: The sieve crosses out composites by their prime factors. Starting at p² and stopping at √n are the two optimisations to explain. In Python, slice assignment on a bytearray does each crossing-out pass in C, which is the difference between 0.3 s and 30 s.
solution.cpp: int countPrimes(int n) { if (n < 3) return 0; vector<char> s(n, 1); s[0] = s[1] = 0; for (long long i = 2; i * i < n; i++) if (s[i]) for (long long j = i * i; j < n; j += i) s[j] = 0; return count(s.begin(), s.end(), 1); }
